summary: Bill line split and duplicate credit attribution caused by mixed org_id in usage postbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported unexpected split charge lines on their March invoice. Two nearly identical invoice line items appear for the same batch embedding job; one line is attributed to the customer org and a second line appears under an internal staging org ID. Credits were applied to the staging line and not the customer line, resulting in an overcharged final invoice.

Impact:
- Invoice shows duplicate/fragmented line items for the same usage window (March 02 03:00 - 03:30 UTC).
- Credits were applied to the wrong line (staging org), leaving BrightCart with an apparent overage of ~$1,240.
- Customer billing team flagged for correction prior to payment. Customer is on Dedicated tier and needs corrected invoice before payment processing.

Environment:
- Prod ingestion pipeline (us-east), dedicated deployment for BrightCart (org_id: org-brightcart-prod).
- Edge postbacks from batch workers (region: us-east-1).

Steps to reproduce / observed behaviour:
1) BrightCart runs a scheduled batch embedding job at 03:05 UTC that posts usage via the usage-postback endpoint.
2) Multiple postback requests for the same job arrived within seconds, some carrying header X-Org-ID: org-brightcart-prod and others carrying X-Org-ID: org-brightcart-staging (a legacy id from an earlier onboarding script).
3) Ingest service accepted both postbacks and created two usage buckets tied to two org identifiers.
4) Billing aggregation produced two invoice lines; credits attached automatically to staging-line because credit memo mapped to org-brightcart-staging first.

Expected behaviour:
- Ingest should canonicalize org ID and reject or normalize mixed org IDs for a single API key, preventing split attribution.
- Credits should map to the primary customer org when both org ids are linked to the same account.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Customer-provided invoice PDF (invoice_2026-03-02_BrightCart.pdf) and CSV extract.
- Ingest logs: usage-postback-2026-03-02.log (contains raw headers showing mixed X-Org-ID values).
- Billing trace: billing-aggregate-2026-03-02.trace (high level aggregation steps).

Business impact:
- Financial: immediate overcharge of $1,240 pending correction.
- Reputational: customer escalated to CSM and finance. BrightCart is a Dedicated customer with SLOs tied to billing accuracy.

Requested outcome:
- Issue the corrective credit and regenerate invoice reflecting a single line for the batch job.
- Identify and patch ingestion flow to canonicalize org IDs per API key and prevent future split attribution.
- Provide RCA and confirmation when reprocessed adjustments appear on account.
comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:34Z - Support (Maya Chen): Received invoice and logs from BrightCart finance. They're requesting a corrected invoice before the March billing cycle closes. Attached invoice PDF and postback log. Escalating to billing team.

2026-03-10T11:05:10Z - Billing (Alejandro Ruiz): Initial triage complete — I can see two distinct org_ids in the postback log. Opening an ingest investigation. Tentatively marking as P2; customer is concerned about timing.

2026-03-10T13:22:47Z - Ingest Eng (Priya Singh): Reproduced on staging: ingestion accepts postbacks with any X-Org-ID header if API key matches, and we index by header value when present. That allows split buckets. Creating PR to normalize to API-key->org mapping and ignore X-Org-ID when it conflicts.

2026-03-11T08:42:19Z - Billing (Alejandro Ruiz): Ran a one-off reaggregation job for affected window. Created credit memo CM-2026-03-11-BC for $1,240 and produced corrected invoice INV-2026-03-11-BC. Sent corrected invoice to customer and finance.
2026-03-11T16:30:05Z - Customer (BrightCart - Lydia Park): Confirmed receipt of corrected invoice and credit memo. Finance will accept and stop payment hold. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

2026-03-12T10:01:58Z - Support (Maya Chen): Closing ticket after confirm from customer. Follow-up: ingest PR merged and deployment scheduled to prod. Added post-deploy alert to detect mixed-org postbacks.
investigation_notes: Ingest service behavior: usage-postback accepts X-Org-ID header and if present treats that header as authoritative even if API key is owned by a different org. This was historical behavior to support certain partner integrations.
Postback logs show batch job had 6 postbacks; 4 used org-brightcart-prod, 2 used org-brightcart-staging. Timestamps within the same window (03:05:22Z - 03:05:31Z).

Billing aggregation iterates over usage rows and groups by org_id found in ingest index. No de-duplication across org IDs was performed. This produced two lines with identical usage details but different org attribution.

Credits service maps credit memos to org ids based on exact org_id match. Credit memo for earlier test runs was tied to org-brightcart-staging and applied to that line because it matched first in aggregation order.
resolution_notes:
Action taken: 1) Issued $1,240 credit memo CM-2026-03-11-BC and regenerated invoice INV-2026-03-11-BC to merge the two lines into the canonical org (org-brightcart-prod). 2) Deployed ingest fix: PR #742 forces API-key->org canonical mapping and drops X-Org-ID header when it conflicts. 3) Backfilled/reaudited the last 30 days of postback records for this customer to ensure no other split attributions exist. 4) Added an alert to detect mixed-org postbacks for a single API key and a runbook to remediate quickly.

Follow-ups: Engineering to monitor alert for one week. Finance to confirm final invoice acceptance by BrightCart. Documented the change in Confluence: billing/postback-runbook.
